interface.title: TransPrimer — Tm-guided exon–exon junction (EEJ) primer design for isoform-specific RT-PCR/qPCR
interface.field: Molecular biology / transcriptomics (RT-PCR and qPCR assay design for alternatively spliced transcripts)
interface.stage_of_work: Experiment planning: designing primers before wet-lab RT-PCR/qPCR
interface.what_it_is_for: Compare a gene's curated RefSeq transcript variants (or transcripts you paste), decide whether a chosen variant can be amplified on its own (unique exon, exon–exon junction only, or infeasible), and design and QC-check primers for it, or design one pair that amplifies all variants for total expression.

data.note: Gene records came from the engine's cached NCBI RefSeq data: human GAPDH, TP53, TCF7L2, BRCA1 and mouse Gapdh all loaded. Custom sequence mode used its built-in 'Load example (GAPDH)' set of 6 transcripts. I also typed in a made-up exon-2-skipping GAPDH isoform (260 nt, built from GAPDH exons 1, 3 and 4). No files were uploaded.

tree.general: Design PCR primers that measure one specific RNA variant of a gene, or all of its variants together, and check that they are specific and well behaved
tree.specific: Use TransPrimer to classify a transcript variant (EEJ-independent, EEJ-dependent or infeasible) and design a conventional, junction-spanning or whole-transcript primer pair that passes primer3 QC

Did not use the '–' / '+' zoom buttons in the cDNA view; I only used 'Full'.
